subject: Zero-trust access provisioning review for private control plane
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alisa K. <alisa@secureid.example.com>
Cc: secops@finco-payments.com
Date: 2028-02-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Zero-trust access provisioning review for private control plane

Team,

Quick kickoff: Finco is moving to a Private Control Plane (VPC + customer-managed control plane) and has asked for a zero-trust identity integration design that covers SAML SSO, SCIM group sync, and short-lived IAM roles for services. I attached a first-pass diagram. High-level asks from Finco:

- Strong separation between control plane auth and tenant workload identities
- Ability to map IdP groups to Redwood RBAC roles via SCIM
- JIT role assumption for ephemeral worker tokens (1h or less)
- Audit evidence (who assumed role, token issuance, rotation events)

Open questions I want us to resolve before the design doc:
1) SCIM: group -> role mapping semantics (nested groups? filtering?)
2) SAML assertions: which attributes do we require (email, groups, eduPersonTargetedID?)
3) Service accounts vs. federated roles: do we require short-lived certificates (mTLS) for control plane-to-operator services?
4) Network constraints: can Finco provide a static egress NAT for callbacks to the Private Control Plane?

Alisa from SecureID is on thread to confirm IdP capabilities and recommended attribute sets. Marcus / Mina / Laura — can you review the attached diagram and flag any impossible asks?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: zero-trust-provisioning-diagram-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alisa K. <alisa@secureid.example.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-02-03T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust access provisioning review for private control plane

Thanks Jordan — quick answers from the IdP side (SecureID):

- SCIM: we support nested groups and incremental syncs. We can send group membership in two modes: full-group list or federated-ids-per-group. For large orgs (Finco fits that profile), we recommend group filters to avoid syncing their entire org.

- SAML attributes: email (NameID), groups (urn:oid:2.5.4.11 or custom), and a persistent subject id (NameQualifier) for auditing. We can also include an assertion for authenticated_at and auth_method.

- Short-lived roles: IdP can emit a signed assertion that Redwood can exchange for a short-lived role token. TTL is configurable; 1 hour is fine.

- JIT provisioning: we support just-in-time provisioning for first-time users and can map using SCIM templates for group->role mapping.

One implementation note: when the control plane is customer-managed (on-prem/VPC), callbacks from Redwood’s control plane services need a routable endpoint and a TLS certificate the customer trusts. Mutual TLS for those endpoints is supported if Finco wants cert pinning.

I'll attach our recommended assertion samples and an example SCIM attribute matrix.

Alisa K.
Solutions Architect, SecureID
[Attachment: scim-attribute-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alisa K. <alisa@secureid.example.com>
Date: 2028-02-04T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust access provisioning review for private control plane

Great details, Alisa — thanks. A few follow-ups from the runtime/infra side:

1) SCIM mapping: we need deterministic group -> RBAC mappings for auditability. Proposal: only allow explicit mappings (no wildcard), and require an admin-signed mapping manifest stored in Finco's control plane (sha256 hash recorded in Redwood audit logs). This avoids accidental privilege escalation from broad group syncs.

2) Role tokens: We'll implement an STS flow where Redwood validates the SAML assertion and issues a short-lived bearer token with scopes encoded (control-plane:admin, control-plane:read, tenant:secrets-access). Tokens will be opaque but we log issuance events to the audit index.

3) Service to service: For operators (e.g., backups, metrics exporters) that run in customer networks, we prefer mTLS client certs with automatic rotation (7d rotation window) over long-lived keys. mTLS certificates can be issued by Redwood's CA if Finco delegates CA trust or by Finco's internal CA if they require autonomy.

4) Network: If Finco cannot provide static egress IPs, we'll need a relay/bastion in their VPC that does. That relay will also host the SAML ACS endpoint for the control plane and accept SCIM push webhooks.

I'll sketch RBAC manifest constraints and share. Marcus

Marcus Lin
Lead Platform Engineer, Redwood

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Alisa K. <alisa@secureid.example.com>
Date: 2028-02-05T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust access provisioning review for private control plane

Adding security POV and compliance checklist items from our side (we looped in Finco secops):

- Audit scope: all SCIM change events, SAML assertion validations, role issuance and assumption, and CA cert rotations must be forwarded to Finco's SIEM (we will support syslog/HTTP ingestion).
- Least privilege: SCIM group sync must include a "pending" state. Any new mapping introduced by SCIM should default to a non-privileged role until manually approved by a Finco admin in the control plane.
- MFA: require MFA assertion in SAML for admin-level role assumption. We recommend rejecting role-assumption if auth_method != "mfa" for admin scopes.
- Emergency breakglass: we need a documented offline token process (signed ephemeral token via DocuSign or KMS-wrapped secret) for incident response; Finco requested this explicitly.

Questions for Finco secops: do you have a preference for SIEM ingestion (syslog over TLS, S3 bucket delivery, or direct API)? secops@finco-payments.com, can you advise?

Mina Haddad
Head of Security Integrations, Redwood Inference
